aws_security.title: AWS Security Transformation
aws_security.subtitle: From 45% to 92% compliance in 8 months
aws_security.overview: Engaged to lead an enterprise security transformation for a large-scale AWS environment, the project required addressing 111+ critical findings across 23 services while maintaining zero downtime and 99.9% service availability throughout.
aws_security.problem: The organization had a 45% compliance score against CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark with over 111 open security findings spanning IAM misconfigurations, unencrypted data at rest, overly permissive security groups, missing logging, and lack of continuous monitoring. Manual remediation attempts were slow, inconsistent, and produced regressions.
aws_security.solution: I architected a phased remediation program with Python/Boto3 automation scripts for systematic hardening, KMS encryption rollout across 89 SNS topics, RDS, EFS, and CloudTrail, IAM restructuring with least-privilege policies and MFA enforcement, Security Group and NACL reviews, and a centralized Security Hub dashboard for ongoing tracking. Each change was validated with Burp Suite and rolled out in maintenance windows to avoid disruption.
aws_security.results: Compliance score improved from 45% to 92% in 8 months. Remediation velocity increased by 70% due to automation. Zero security incidents occurred during the process. The organization now has continuous compliance monitoring with automated drift detection and an incident response playbook in place.
aws_security.takeaway1: Automation is the only way to remediate at scale without regressions — manual tickets don't hold up across 23 services
aws_security.takeaway2: Phased rollouts with rollback plans are non-negotiable in production environments with strict uptime requirements
aws_security.takeaway3: Security Hub as a single pane of glass dramatically accelerates stakeholder communication and prioritization
aws_security.takeaway4: KMS encryption and IAM hardening yield the highest compliance impact for the effort invested

aws_cost.title: AWS FinOps Analysis
aws_cost.subtitle: $700–760/month in optimization identified across a drifted 4-year AWS account
aws_cost.overview: Engaged to run an end-to-end FinOps analysis of a B2B SaaS platform's AWS account — averaging roughly $2,830 per month with no cost governance, a 4-year-old drifted CDK codebase, and significant infrastructure sprawl.
aws_cost.problem: The account had no cost governance in place. A CDK TypeScript codebase four years old had drifted significantly from live infrastructure: some resources — ECS, ECR, CloudFront — were still IaC-managed, while others, including RDS, ElastiCache, the VPC, and multiple Elastic IPs, were entirely unmanaged with no audit trail. Leadership's initial expectation was that all optimizations could ship within 48 hours.
aws_cost.solution: I ran a full account inventory across more than 10 service categories and a drift analysis between the CDK codebase and live infrastructure. That surfaced the critical anomaly: a ScheduledFargateTask cron set to run every minute, launching up to 9 Fargate tasks per minute, 24/7, across all three environments — likely running unnoticed since 2022. I delivered a 5-report suite: an executive inventory, a FinOps assessment with a structured 13-week remediation plan, an engineering discovery guide, a technical CDK analysis, and a supporting addendum — resetting the 48-hour assumption into a realistic, phased plan.
aws_cost.results: The analysis identified $700–760 per month in actionable optimization, with the highest-priority tier alone accounting for $513–523/month — about 18% of the total bill. The full inventory covered 5 EC2 instances, 4 RDS instances, 3 ElastiCache clusters, 9 load balancers reducible to 3, 21 ECR repositories holding 7,753 stale images with zero lifecycle policies, 29 S3 buckets, 3 CloudFront distributions, and 23 Elastic IPs — 20 of them unattached, costing roughly $73/month for nothing. Leadership accepted the realistic 13-week plan in place of the original 48-hour expectation.
aws_cost.takeaway1: Infrastructure drift compounds silently — a 4-year-old IaC codebase that's stopped tracking reality is itself a cost and risk finding, not just a technical debt note
aws_cost.takeaway2: A single misconfigured cron can quietly burn resources 24/7 for years — automated scheduling needs the same review rigor as application code
aws_cost.takeaway3: Resetting unrealistic timeline expectations is part of the deliverable — a credible multi-week plan beats a rushed promise that can't actually be met
aws_cost.takeaway4: Lifecycle policies are the highest-leverage, lowest-risk fix available — cleaning up thousands of unmanaged container images carries zero operational risk and meaningful savings

cicd_security.title: CI/CD Maturity Assessment
cicd_security.subtitle: Closing the one gap that mattered across a 35-repo engineering org
cicd_security.overview: Ran a structured CI/CD maturity assessment across a 35-repository enterprise financial services GitHub organization, surfacing a critical deployment-automation gap and delivering a modernization proposal that leadership accepted.
cicd_security.problem: The organization actually had a solid CI foundation — automated tests, security scans, and container builds ran on every pull request. The real gap was further downstream: there was no automated deployment trigger connecting approved, tested code to an actual environment deployment. Releases were fully manual, unscheduled, and dependent on individual availability. Quality gates existed but were configured report-only, so a failing scan or test didn't block a merge or a deployment. One service group, the AWS Lambda functions, had no CI pipeline at all — no tests, no scans, no build process.
cicd_security.solution: I built an automated inventory across all 35 repositories covering pipeline coverage, branch protection, and primary language, then deep-reviewed 7 of the most actively maintained repos end to end — full pipeline configuration and git history. I ran a structured working session with the client's engineering and delivery teams to validate the findings against real operational constraints, then scoped a proposal: automated deployment triggers on merge to the stable branch, release and environment traceability, enforcement-grade quality gates that actually block on failure instead of just reporting, and a foundational CI/CD pipeline for the previously uncovered Lambda services. Separately, in the same engagement, I found a production Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 cluster that had drifted outside IaC management and resolved it with a CDK stack matching the original cluster identifier under a retain policy, restoring IaC ownership with zero data disruption.
cicd_security.results: The 35-repo inventory and 7-repo deep review were delivered, and leadership accepted the modernization proposal. The Aurora cluster was brought back under CDK management with zero data disruption, and the infrastructure drift was fully documented.
cicd_security.takeaway1: A CI pipeline that runs checks isn't the same as a CD pipeline that acts on them — report-only quality gates are a false sense of security
cicd_security.takeaway2: The highest-value finding in an assessment is often not the exotic one — a missing deploy trigger across 35 repos mattered more than any individual pipeline's sophistication
cicd_security.takeaway3: Scoping matters as much as the findings — staying inside the boundaries of infrastructure you actually own keeps a proposal credible and actionable
cicd_security.takeaway4: IaC drift recovery — bringing a live resource back under management with a retain policy — is a precise, high-stakes operation; zero data disruption is the only acceptable outcome

ai_platform.title: Multi-Tenant AI Agent Platform
ai_platform.subtitle: Zero open ports. Per-tenant isolation. Production AI agents.
ai_platform.overview: Designed and deployed a production multi-tenant platform hosting OpenClaw, an AI gateway connecting LLMs to messaging and productivity tools, with zero open inbound ports and per-tenant isolation enforced from the network layer up.
ai_platform.problem: The platform needed to run OpenClaw for multiple isolated tenants simultaneously, each with its own credentials and tool integrations, completely separated from every other tenant. The naive approach — open SSH ports and config files on a shared EC2 instance — wasn't viable for production: it exposed credentials, created an unacceptable attack surface, and made onboarding and secret rotation manual and error-prone at scale.
ai_platform.solution: I built the platform as 7 Pulumi TypeScript components — networking, secrets, IAM, storage, compute, observability, and a dedicated access component for per-tenant IAM — with one isolated stack per tenant. SSH is closed entirely; all access goes through SSM Session Manager port-forwarding, so there are zero open inbound ports. Credentials flow exclusively through Secrets Manager into each tenant's IAM instance profile, EBS and EFS are encrypted at rest, and a CloudWatch alarm acts as a kill switch, auto-stopping any instance that sustains over 90% CPU for 15 minutes. An onboarding script automates tenant provisioning end to end, and a hardening script runs non-destructive security audits against live instances. Nine security controls are documented and tracked — eight enforced by default, the ninth a deliberate, documented exception rather than an oversight.
ai_platform.results: The platform shipped across 10 merged PRs in a single foundation-and-security milestone, with zero open inbound ports maintained across every tenant. It's been deployed across multiple internal tenants, including my own production use, spanning more than one AWS region. Secret rotation applies in roughly 10 seconds with no infrastructure redeploy required.
ai_platform.takeaway1: SSM port-forwarding eliminates the open-SSH attack surface entirely without sacrificing operational access — zero open ports is achievable in production without workflow pain
ai_platform.takeaway2: Per-tenant Secrets Manager paths with isolated IAM give strong separation, and credential rotation measured in seconds instead of a redeploy changes how often you're willing to rotate
ai_platform.takeaway3: Documenting a deliberate exception is more trustworthy than claiming blanket compliance — security maturity shows in what you chose not to do, and why
ai_platform.takeaway4: Automating onboarding and audits as first-class scripts, not one-off runbooks, is what makes multi-tenant operations sustainable past the first few tenants

compliance.title: Cybersecurity Compliance Program
compliance.subtitle: 29% → 87% in 6 weeks across 5 security frameworks
compliance.overview: Delivered a comprehensive cybersecurity compliance program for a multi-carrier insurance platform serving major global insurers. Starting from a formal gap analysis, the engagement covered 49 security controls across 10 domains — achieving 87% automated compliance in under 6 weeks while managing 5 simultaneous insurer security questionnaires and deploying CDK TypeScript infrastructure that eliminated the platform's highest-risk exposures.
compliance.problem: The platform had a 29% baseline compliance score (14/49 controls passing) against ISO 27001, CIS Controls v8, and LFPDPPP (Mexico's data privacy law). Five major global insurers were simultaneously conducting security questionnaires — delays put contract value at risk. The baseline audit surfaced 5 critical and 11 high severity findings: CloudTrail was completely absent (zero API activity ever recorded), a hardcoded AES encryption key was embedded in source code and shared across all 7 tenant variants, the DLP tool had been purchased over a year prior but never configured — leaving zero data protection in place, the bastion host SSH was open to the internet (0.0.0.0/0) in CDK, and CI/CD pipelines ran under an AdministratorAccess IAM user with no MFA. No security policies, no gap analysis, and no audit evidence existed.
compliance.solution: I led the program across three parallel tracks. Infrastructure: CDK TypeScript managing 5 stacks (~35–40 resources) — VPC with WAF v2 (OWASP Top 10, SQLi, KnownBadInputs rule sets), EC2 Windows/IIS, RDS SQL Server, S3 with encryption and lifecycle policies, and a dedicated security stack enabling GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector v2, CloudTrail with CloudWatch alarms, and AWS Backup with daily RDS snapshots. RDP access proxied exclusively via SSM Session Manager port-forwarding — no direct desktop port exposed. Bastion SSH hardening CDK fix delivered (pending team deployment). GitHub Actions OIDC replaced the AdministratorAccess IAM user entirely. Documentation: 12+ formal deliverables authored including Information Security Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Incident Response Plan, Disaster Recovery Plan, gap analysis, and remediation roadmap — all audit-ready. Questionnaire management: all 5 insurer questionnaires actively managed concurrently, with controls mapped systematically to each insurer's evidence requirements.
compliance.results: Compliance score rose from 29% to 87% in under 6 weeks — 13 of 15 automated controls continuously passing as tracked weekly. 30+ RDS backup jobs completed successfully. GitHub Actions OIDC eliminated the AdministratorAccess IAM user and all long-lived deploy credentials. RDP access exclusively via SSM Session Manager with IAM MFA enforced at session level. Twelve-plus formal policies and procedures delivered, audit-ready. Entire infrastructure managed as code in CDK TypeScript.
compliance.takeaway1: CDK TypeScript enables compliance-as-code — WAF rules, GuardDuty, and CloudTrail configuration are version-controlled and provide an auditable evidence trail out of the box
compliance.takeaway2: SSM Session Manager replacing open RDP/SSH ports is the single change that reduces the most attack surface with the least operational impact on the development team
compliance.takeaway3: Managing compliance documentation and insurer questionnaires concurrently demands a systematic control-mapping approach — each control needs evidence artifacts, not just enablement
compliance.takeaway4: GitHub Actions OIDC over long-lived IAM credentials requires one CDK stack and eliminates an entire class of credential leakage risk from CI/CD pipelines
